A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Bernoulli bandits, combination locks, Wordle, RiverSwim, and informative-action bandits, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds customer-service, DeepSeek-R1, and comparative token-efficiency results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a task-specific LLM prior-generation step for customer service, optionally instructed to include the known solution among its hypotheses (Section 4.1.2 and Appendix H.2.2). The three-role PSRL procedure and existing LLM-IDS method remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds customer-service issues from Tajwar et al., requiring agents to ask unrestricted natural-language questions or propose solutions to simulated customers. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's constrained guessing tasks and numerical environments. The original tasks remain.

E2.justification: The comparison algorithms remain unchanged. DeepSeek-R1 supplies additional model configurations, while customer service uses the existing Reflexion and ICRL baselines. Although v2 Figure 8 omits ICPI's Wordle curve, Section 4.3 still reports its ten trials and failure to obtain nonzero reward; its evaluation has not been removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include 20-turn customer-service interactions with GPT-4o customer and judge models, two prior-construction conditions, DeepSeek-R1 configurations, and regret evaluated against mean token consumption. Retained settings largely persist. v2 also removes v1's conflicting 60% RiverSwim advancement footnote while retaining the 35% description; unchanged curves do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds prior-support sensitivity analysis for customer service, tests robustness to using DeepSeek-R1 on the guessing tasks, and compares token efficiency against Reflexion and ICRL (Appendices B.2, E, and G). Existing temperature analyses, RiverSwim failure investigations, and IDS experiments are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report repeated trials and identify shaded uncertainty as one standard error. Existing trial counts remain unchanged, and added evaluations follow the same reporting practice. v2's statistical-significance assertions do not introduce a specified significance test or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds customer-service results, DeepSeek-R1 results, and comparative token-consumption curves. For example, Figure 8 reports final Wordle regret around 2.6 for PSRL with R1 versus approximately 4.65 with GPT-4o; these are different backbone conditions, not a same-setting improvement between versions. Most original plots, including Bernoulli, RiverSwim, and IDS results, are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 removes v1 Section 4.1's explicit statement that the best-known PSRL regret bound lies within O-tilde(sqrt(H)) of the strongest lower bound. The underlying MDP and IDS mathematics remain essentially unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: implementing existing PSRL subroutines with LLMs can yield efficient exploration, and constituent model capability matters. The added experiments support this contribution without redefining its central claim. LLM-IDS was already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through observed prior-misspecification failures, arguments that structured exploration contributes beyond stronger reasoning models, and explanations of token overhead through explicit enumeration of candidate lock codes. It also explicitly anticipates longer-horizon Bernoulli failures at insufficient sampling temperatures. Existing stochastic-planning and Thompson-sampling limitations remain in Appendices D and F.

D1.justification: Appendix H.2.2 supplies customer-service environment, sampling, customer, judge, and prior-generator prompts, alongside a dataset location. v2 also documents manual prompt iteration and adds a reproducibility statement. Existing PSRL, IDS, and baseline prompts and the numerical cost tables are essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Tajwar et al., Silver and Sutton, Gittins, Freund and Schapire, and Xu et al. (2023), while removing Schaul et al.'s policy-churn reference. The broader research positioning is retained; most related work moves to Appendix A. Klissarov et al.'s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: experiments and discussion are integrated, RiverSwim precedes the guessing tasks, related work moves to Appendix A, and the detailed limitations and IDS material move to Appendices D and F. The conclusion is condensed and a reproducibility statement is added, although much underlying prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column conference layout. Figure 1 changes from stacked to horizontal panels, numerous figures are regrouped or relocated, and the Wordle plot receives new curves and a revised legend. Customer-service, R1, and token-efficiency displays are added, while the existing cost tables are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation by testing another backbone on the guessing tasks, comparing baseline token consumption, and directly examining prior-support sensitivity. These address gaps in v1's evidence. The practical extension remains limited: customer-service interactions and judgments are simulated, and the strongest PSRL condition includes the dataset's correct solution among its prior hypotheses. The additions improve the paper without resolving its established stochastic-planning limitations.
